SpaceX is asking Cochise County to keep its December 9 public hearing on schedule. Here’s what the company says its proposed project would deliver:

• More local tax revenue: Estimated benefits include up to $103 million annually in property taxes and a one-time county sales tax benefit of up to $250 million. 

• Protection for existing electricity customers: Proposed financial guarantees and separate cost accounting would keep the project’s electricity and infrastructure costs with SpaceX.

• Massive battery storage: Around 24 GWh, equivalent to roughly four hours at full load. The campus could reduce grid demand during periods of stress.

• Water-conscious cooling: Dry, closed-loop cooling without routine evaporative cooling or industrial groundwater pumping. Initial filling would use treated wastewater or trucked water.

• No operating gas power plant proposed: Normal operations would use grid electricity. Generators would provide backup for critical systems.

• Emergency preparedness funded by SpaceX: The company accepts all six local emergency planning recommendations at its expense, including emergency plans, training and responder access.

• Traffic improvements: SpaceX commits to funding an independent traffic review, with plans including worker shuttles, staggered shifts and required road improvements.

• Wildlife and night-sky protections: Plans include downward-facing lighting, bird-safe building features, wildlife-friendly fencing and markers on new overhead lines.

• Military coordination: SpaceX says it will consult Fort Huachuca and the Electronic Proving Ground and address written concerns before the first building permit.
